title: Declare what every URN-carrying test proves

facts.note: Any test file carrying a URN header, in any stack and whether newly written, edited or already existing. The obligation is stack-neutral; only the bundled detector (bun_tester_discipline_detector) is Bun/JS/TS-specific, which limits automated coverage, not applicability.

values: URN header present but no `// Acceptance:` and no `// Train:` header
facts.note: Presence path: a header scan of the file content; already realized for Bun suites by bun_tester_discipline_detector and directly readable in any test file.

values: URN header present with only a `// Train:` header on a test that is not a journey/E2E test
facts.note: Binding-kind path: the Train header is header-scannable now, but classifying the test as journey/E2E or not needs a new observer (e.g. test-tier/path classification) or LLM judgment. The current detector accepts any Train header, so this case is not caught structurally.

values: Acceptance/Train header present but test may not exercise/assert the bound subject
facts.note: Truthfulness path: applies to every bound URN-carrying test, including valid-looking headers; only reviewer/LLM judgment can compare stimulus and witness with the bound obligation.

fires: Presence: a test file carries a URN header but has neither an `// Acceptance: acc:…` nor a `// Train: …` header
Binding kind: a URN-carrying test that is not a journey/E2E test is bound only by a `// Train: …` header (fires regardless of whether the test exercises or asserts that train)
Truthfulness: a URN-carrying test declares an Acceptance or Train binding whose subject the test does not exercise or whose outcome it does not assert
Truthfulness: a binding was selected, changed or invented only so the test becomes attributable
doesNotFire: A test file with no URN header (owned by test-carries-urn-identity)
Presence and binding-kind paths: a journey/E2E test with a `// Train: …` header (truthfulness review still applies)
Checking whether the named acceptance exists in the plan graph (owned by acceptance-resolves-to-declared)

given: A test file carries a URN identity header
when: The test is written, changed or reviewed
then: Declare beside the URN the plan obligation the test actually proves: `// Acceptance: acc:…`, or `// Train: …` only for a journey/E2E test.
prefer: Derive the binding from the plan artifact the test proves: the declared acceptance whose behavior the file exercises and asserts, or the declared train the journey actually walks
Use that exact plan identity: `// Acceptance: acc:<domain>:<acceptance-id>` or `// Train: train:<domain>:<journey>`
avoid: Picking any resolvable acceptance merely to satisfy coverage
Changing the claimed binding to match a test that proves different behavior (rebinding for attribution); correcting a stale binding to the obligation the test truly proves is the fix, not this
Selecting or inventing a binding (new acceptance or train) merely to make an orphaned test bind or be attributable
unless: A `Train:` binding satisfies the rule for journey and E2E tests, when the journey actually proves that train
why: A URN says which test this is; the binding says which obligation it discharges, and only that closes the loop the gate reads. The binding is a claim: truthful only if the test exercises the declared subject and asserts its outcome. A convenient but unrelated resolvable acceptance creates false coverage while still passing the structural detector. Train bindings exist because journeys prove a train; forcing an acceptance would push authors to invent linter-only acceptances that pollute the plan graph.
evidence: Every URN-carrying test file has an `Acceptance:` or `Train:` field beside the URN (bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no finding for Bun suites)
Any test bound only by `Train:` is a journey/E2E test
The test stimulus exercises the bound subject
The test's behavioral witness proves the bound obligation rather than an adjacent implementation detail
verifier_detail: Detector: bun_tester_discipline_detector (validator). Requires an `Acceptance:` or `Train:` field beside the URN header.

Accepted forms: acceptance_binding `// Acceptance: acc:…` (names the obligation the test discharges); train_binding `// Train: …` (alternative for a journey test, which proves a train rather than a single acceptance).
Files with no URN are skipped — that finding belongs to `test-carries-urn-identity`.
Whether the named acceptance EXISTS is a plan-graph question this per-file detector cannot answer; out of scope here (see acceptance-resolves-to-declared).

Truthfulness (stimulus exercises subject, witness proves obligation) is not structurally detectable: a convenient existing acceptance bound to an unrelated case creates false coverage while satisfying the structural detector. Requires reviewer/LLM judgment.

Two binding kinds are accepted on purpose: a journey test legitimately proves a train rather than a single acceptance, and forcing every test to name an acceptance would push authors to invent one, polluting the plan graph with acceptances that exist only to satisfy a linter.
Disposition: strict for this rule. Bun realization: atdd-bun fails on every finding of this rule; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

Binding-kind check: the structural detector accepts any `Train:` header; whether the file is a journey/E2E test (the only case where Train alone satisfies the rule) must be established by a test-tier classifier or reviewer judgment.

splitSuggestion.then: A declared Acceptance/Train binding must name the subject the test actually exercises and whose outcome it asserts; never select or invent a binding merely to make a test attributable.

sharedNodes.text: strict: the enforcing gate fails on every finding of the rule; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Presence of a binding (structural, detector-checked) and truthfulness of the binding (reviewer/LLM-judged) are independent obligations; suggest a separate convention tester.binding-truthful.
additions.justification: Rule 2: one obligation in `then`; truthfulness kept in avoid/prefer/evidence as the same decision.

additions.justification: Source S006/S012/S037 restrict Train to journey/E2E tests; without this case a Train-only non-journey test escaped activation.

additions.justification: Prevents misreading S032 as forbidding truthful correction; follows from S023/S025 (derive binding from what the test proves). Adds no waiver.
